scope: Three alternating same-host identical-guest-program pairs. PCEMU CPU/JIT-only RAM harness versus QEMU full PC TCG. Supervisor 4KiB identity paging; shuffled dependent pointer loads. Different timing mechanisms; not Windows/application performance or raw host RAM latency.

limitations: Original pointer-chasing benchmark, not lmbench results or a port of its source.
PCEMU uses CPU/JIT directly, without Machine/device polling. QEMU runs the full PC model. Ratios apply only to these harnesses, not overall emulator or Windows rankings.
PCEMU times inside I/O handlers; QEMU uses host socket receipt. Scheduling/transport error is not calibrated; all measured intervals exceed 0.1 seconds.
Fixed case order, deterministic permutation, supervisor mode, 4KiB identity paging; no user-mode, page-fault, MMIO, SMC or streaming-bandwidth measurement.
Working-set span is sparse for page-stride rings: only one 32-bit pointer per page is read; this is not DRAM bandwidth.
Warmup traverses the exact loop before timing; page tables and rings initialize outside intervals; dispatch and native translation guards remain measured.
Three pairs on one host without confidence intervals; raw timings/load retained. Native coverage is counted instructions, not host time.
